examples.en: I practice alone while looking at a piano manual.
This guitar manual suits beginners well.

examples.ko: 서점에서 요리 교본을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a cooking guidebook at the bookstore.

examples.ko: 이 책은 운전 교본처럼 설명이 쉬워요.
examples.en: This book explains things easily, like a driving manual.

examples.ko: 교본대로 따라 했는데도 잘 안 됐어요.
examples.en: I followed the manual exactly, but it did not work.
The teacher teaches with a manual they wrote themselves.

explain: 학교 교과서보다는 악기, 운동, 요리처럼 기술을 처음 배우는 책에 써요. 학교 수업에서는 '교과서'라고 하고, 교본은 '기본을 익히는 책'에 가까워요. 비유로 '모범'이라는 뜻으로 '교본 같은 사람'이라고 하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I tried cooking by following a cooking manual.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기술 이름 뒤에 붙여 어떤 기술을 배우는 책인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put after a skill name to say what the book teaches.

phrases.en: I learned drawing by myself with a manual.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선생님 없이 책으로 익힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when learning from a book without a teacher.

phrases.en: Please open your math textbook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 수업에서 쓰는 책이에요. '교본'과 구분해서 알아 두세요.
phrases.nuance_en: The book used in school classes; distinguish it from 교본.

explain_en: Rather than a school textbook, it is used for books that teach a skill from the start, such as an instrument, sport or cooking. In school lessons Koreans say 교과서. Figuratively, 교본 같은 사람 can describe a person who is a perfect model.

en: school record (grades counted for college admission)

examples.ko: 내신 성적이 좋아야 원하는 대학에 가요.
examples.en: You need good school record grades to get into the college you want.

examples.ko: 시험이 내신에 반영된다고 해서 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: I worked hard because the exam counts toward my school record.
Because of school record grades, my friends study even during vacation.
I changed cram schools to raise my school record grade.
I'm more worried about my school record than the CSAT.

examples.ko: 내신 시험이 다음 주라서 도서관에 갔어요.
examples.en: My school exam is next week, so I went to the library.

explain: 대학 입시 이야기에서 나오는 말이에요. 학교 안에서 받은 성적이 내신이고, 한 번에 보는 '수능'과 구분해요. 학교 시험 점수 자체는 그냥 '성적'이라고 해요. '내신이 좋다/나쁘다', '내신 등급'으로 말해요.

phrases.en: My school record grade went up, so I'm happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 성적을 등급으로 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing used when talking about school grades as ranked levels.

phrases.en: My school record is good, so I got a strong recommendation too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내신'을 평가할 때 '좋다/나쁘다'를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 'good/bad' to evaluate someone's school record.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a good school record

phrases.en: Managing your school record is important for high school students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험과 수행평가로 학교 성적을 챙기는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to keeping your in-school grades on track through exams and assignments.

explain_en: This word comes up when talking about college admission. Grades earned inside school are 내신, set apart from the one-time 수능 exam. A school test score by itself is simply 성적. It is used as 내신이 좋다/나쁘다 and 내신 등급.

examples.en: I ignored my homework and only played games.
You can't abandon your responsibility and run away.
The child flung their bag down in the entryway and left it.
Word got around that he's someone who abandoned his family.
They do half the work and then just drop it.
Don't blow off your promise to a friend.

explain: 물건을 홱 던져 버린다는 뜻도 있지만, 일, 책임, 사람을 돌보지 않고 저버릴 때 더 많이 써요. 물리적으로 거칠게 던지는 동작은 '내동댕이치다'가 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: He abandoned his family and left.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내팽개치다'보다 조금 짧고 뜻은 거의 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly shorter form with almost the same meaning as '내팽개치다'.

phrases.example: 일을 내팽개치고 놀러 가면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not drop your work and go out to play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해야 할 일을 책임지지 않고 버려 둘 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for abandoning work you should be doing.

phrases.en: Even if it's hard, don't give up on your studies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형으로 말리거나 당부할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to advise or urge someone not to do it.

explain_en: It can mean flinging something away, but it is used more for abandoning work, responsibility or people without caring for them. For a rough physical throw, '내동댕이치다' fits better.

examples.en: My rank went up a lot on this exam.
My rank is tenth in the class.
I decided not to compare ranks with my friend.

examples.ko: 등수에 너무 신경 쓰면 공부가 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you worry too much about rank, studying gets hard.

examples.ko: 달리기 시합에서 등수 안에 들지 못했어요.
examples.en: I didn't place in the running race.

examples.ko: 선생님이 등수 대신 점수만 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us only our scores instead of ranks.

explain: '몇 등이냐'를 말할 때의 그 숫자를 가리켜요. 시험, 달리기, 대회 순위에 두루 쓰고, 학교 성적 순위는 '석차'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 공부를 안 했더니 등수가 많이 떨어졌어요.
phrases.en: I didn't study, so my rank dropped a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순위가 낮아졌다는 뜻이고, 반대는 '등수가 오르다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the rank went down; the opposite is 등수가 오르다.

phrases.en: The teacher ranked us by our running times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기록이나 점수를 보고 순서를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for deciding order based on records or scores.

phrases.en: What place did you get in this contest?
phrases.nuance_ko: 순위를 물을 때 쓰는 가장 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest way to ask about someone's ranking.

explain_en: It refers to the number in 'what place did you get'. It works for exams, races and contests, and a school grade ranking is also called '석차'.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 오월 말에 모내기를 해요.
examples.en: This village transplants rice seedlings at the end of May.
Once the rice planting is done, the paddies turn green.

examples.ko: 비가 알맞게 와서 올해는 물 걱정 없이 모내기를 마쳤어요.
examples.en: The rain came at just the right time, so this year we finished rice planting without worrying about water.
Many hands are needed during the rice-planting season.
During rice planting, neighbors help one another.
These days they plant rice seedlings by machine, so it is much faster.

explain: 볍씨를 키운 모를 논에 옮겨 심는 일이에요. 보통 늦봄에서 초여름에 하고, 그때를 '모내기철'이라고 해요. 동사 '모내다'보다 '모내기를 하다'처럼 명사로 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 비가 온 뒤에 마을 사람들이 모내기를 했어요.
phrases.en: The villagers planted rice seedlings after the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 일을 말할 때 가장 기본이 되는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to talk about this work.

phrases.en: During rice-planting season the countryside is very busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모내기를 하는 늦봄에서 초여름을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to late spring to early summer, when rice is planted.

phrases.example: 모내기가 끝나서 이제 좀 쉴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Rice planting is done, so we can rest a little now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝났음을 말할 때 주어로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as the subject when the work is finished.

explain_en: It is the work of moving young rice seedlings into the paddy. It usually happens from late spring to early summer, and that period is called '모내기철'. People more often use the noun, as in '모내기를 하다', than the verb '모내다'.

examples.en: I majored in physics at university.
The physics exam is tomorrow, so I am worried.
Physics is hard but fun.
That professor is famous in the field of physics.
My younger sibling wants to go to the physics department.
I borrowed a physics book from the library.

explain: 물리학, 화학, 수학처럼 '-학'으로 끝나는 말은 공부하는 분야 이름이에요. 물리학을 연구하는 사람은 '물리학자', 대학의 학과는 '물리학과'예요. 보통 '물리학을 전공하다', '물리학을 공부하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: He is a famous physicist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물리학을 연구하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who studies physics.

phrases.en: My older sister attends the physics department at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교의 학과 이름으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as the name of a university department.

phrases.en: I want to major in physics.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학에서 주로 공부하는 분야를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the field you mainly study at university.

explain_en: Words ending in '-학' such as 물리학, 화학 and 수학 are names of fields of study. A person who researches physics is a '물리학자', and the university department is '물리학과'. It is usually used as in '물리학을 전공하다' or '물리학을 공부하다'.

examples.en: I studied art history at university.
In art history class, we learn about famous painters.

examples.ko: 이 책은 서양 미술사를 쉽게 설명해 줘요.
examples.en: This book explains Western art history in an easy way.
If you know art history, museums are more fun.

examples.ko: 언니는 미술사 교수님이 되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My older sister wants to become an art history professor.
I signed up for a lecture on Korean art history.

explain: '미술'은 그림이나 조각 같은 작품 자체이고, '미술사'는 그것이 시대에 따라 어떻게 변했는지를 연구하는 학문이에요. 같은 방식으로 '음악사', '문학사'처럼 뒤에 '사'를 붙여요. '서양 미술사', '한국 미술사'처럼 앞에 나라나 지역을 붙여 구별해요.

phrases.en: I am reading a book on Western art history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역 이름을 앞에 붙여 범위를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A region name is put in front to show the scope.

phrases.en: I attended a Korean art history lecture at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 작품이 시대별로 어떻게 변했는지 배울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for studying how Korean art changed through eras.

phrases.en: My older sister majored in art history at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 주로 공부하는 분야를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the main field you study at school.

explain_en: 미술 is the art itself, while 미술사 is the field that studies how art changed over time. The same pattern works for 음악사 and 문학사. Add the region in front to specify, as in 서양 미술사 or 한국 미술사.

examples.ko: 할머니 동네에는 학생이 열 명뿐인 분교가 있어요.
examples.en: Grandma's village has a branch school with only ten students.
The teacher worked at a branch school on an island.

examples.ko: 산골 분교는 졸업생이 몇 명 안 돼요.
examples.en: The mountain-village branch school has only a few graduates.
That university set up a branch campus in the countryside.

examples.ko: 분교 아이들은 한 교실에서 같이 공부해요.
examples.en: The children at the branch school study together in one classroom.

examples.ko: 인구가 줄어서 분교가 문을 닫는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many branch schools are closing because the population is shrinking.

explain: '분교'는 본교에서 떨어진 곳에 따로 세운 작은 학교예요. 한국에서는 시골이나 섬의 작은 초등학교를 말할 때 자주 써요. 대학교에서는 '캠퍼스'라고도 하지만 '분교'는 원래 학교의 한 부분이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 저는 어릴 때 섬의 분교에 다녔어요.
phrases.en: When I was young, I attended a branch school on an island.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에 다닌다는 뜻으로 '다니다'와 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 다니다 to mean attending the school.

phrases.en: Branch schools in the countryside have few students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분교가 있는 곳을 말할 때 '시골'을 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 시골 in front to say where the branch school is.

phrases.en: The branch school closed because the students decreased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생 수가 줄어든 시골 학교 이야기에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard when talking about rural schools losing students.

explain_en: 분교 is a small school set up away from the main school. In Korea it often refers to tiny elementary schools in the countryside or on islands. For universities, 캠퍼스 is also used, but 분교 feels more like a part of the original school.

en: to be winding; to be zigzag

examples.en: The handwriting is so crooked that it's hard to read.
My teeth are crooked, so I'm getting braces.

examples.ko: 그림 속 집의 선이 너무 비뚤비뚤하네요.
examples.en: The lines of the house in this picture are so crooked.
It's my first time writing, so it's crooked, but that's okay.

examples.ko: 줄이 비뚤비뚤한 걸 보니 급하게 섰나 봐요.
examples.en: The line is crooked, so they must have lined up in a hurry.
I lined up the shoes that had been left crookedly.

explain: '삐뚤삐뚤하다'와 같은 뜻인데 조금 더 부드러운 느낌이에요. 글씨, 선, 치아처럼 줄지어 있는 것이 고르지 않을 때 잘 어울려요. 명사 앞에서는 '비뚤비뚤한 글씨'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Crooked handwriting is fine too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 '-한' 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-한' form describes the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The line is crooked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 모습을 말하는 해요체 현재형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The present-tense polite form, describing how things look now.

phrases.en: This line isn't crooked; it's straight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'로 부정할 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form using '-지 않다'.

explain_en: It means the same as '삐뚤삐뚤하다' but sounds a little softer. It fits things lined up unevenly, such as handwriting, lines and teeth. Before a noun, say '비뚤비뚤한 글씨'.

en: to make succeed; to bring to success

examples.ko: 저는 이 사업을 꼭 성공시킬 거예요.
examples.en: I will definitely make this business a success.
The team members made the project a success.
I worked all night to make the experiment succeed.
What's the secret to making a small shop succeed?
Everyone works hard to make the plan succeed.
If you pull off the event, you get a bonus.

explain: '성공하다'는 일이 잘 되는 것이고, '성공시키다'는 내가 노력해서 일을 성공하게 만드는 것이에요. 목적어에 일, 사업, 계획 같은 것이 와요. 사람 자신이 목적어로 오는 말은 아니에요.

phrases.en: I really want to make this event a success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 잘 되게 하고 싶은 바람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses a wish to make something succeed.

phrases.en: I prepared hard in order to make the plan succeed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to state a purpose.

phrases.en: We couldn't make that business a success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노력했지만 성공하게 하지 못했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you tried but did not manage to make it succeed.

explain_en: '성공하다' means something goes well. 성공시키다 means you make an effort so that a task succeeds. The object is a thing like a project, business or plan, not the person themself.

examples.en: I use this expression often in real life.
I solved problems connected to real life.
I learned how math is used in real life.
I study practical English conversation.
Real life is very different from books.

examples.ko: 실생활에 도움이 되는 정보를 알려 줘요.
examples.en: They share information that helps in daily life.

explain: 실생활은 책이나 이론과 구분해서 진짜 살아가는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 일상생활과 비슷하지만, 배운 것이 실제로 쓰이느냐를 말하는 느낌이 더 강해요. '실생활 영어', '실생활에서 쓰다'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I tried using the expressions I learned in real life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배운 것을 실제로 쓰는 상황을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used for situations where learning is put to real use.

phrases.en: I want to learn practical everyday English.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실생활' 뒤에 과목이나 말을 붙여 쓸모 있는 내용을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put after a subject to mean practical, usable content.

phrases.en: This class is helpful in real life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배운 것이 실제로 쓸모 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what you learn is actually useful.
phrases.en_equiv: to be useful in real life

explain_en: 실생활 is used to contrast real living with books or theory. It is close to 일상생활, but it leans more toward whether what you learned is actually used. It shows up often in phrases like 실생활 영어 and 실생활에서 쓰다.

examples.en: The students do their practical training at a hospital.
I practiced hands-on what I learned in class.
The time we practice cooking hands-on is the most fun.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에는 현장에서 실습할 기회가 있어요.
examples.en: This semester there is a chance to train in the field.

examples.ko: 이론을 배우고 나서 바로 실습하면 더 잘 기억나요.
examples.en: If you practice right after learning the theory, you remember it better.
She talked about her experience of student teaching at an elementary school.

explain: '연습하다'는 잘하려고 되풀이하는 것이고, 실습하다는 배운 이론을 실제 현장이나 도구로 해 보는 것이에요. 학교·병원·공장의 수업이나 훈련에 주로 쓰고 '현장 실습', '실습생'처럼 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: The university student does on-site training at a company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 일하는 곳에서 해 보는 실습이라는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing meaning hands-on practice at a real workplace.

phrases.en: A new trainee came to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실습하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who is doing practical training.

phrases.example: 수업에서 배운 것을 직접 해 봤어요.
phrases.en: I tried out for myself what I learned in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '실습하다' 대신 쉽게 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday alternative to 실습하다.

explain_en: '연습하다' is repeating something to get better; 실습하다 is trying out learned theory in a real setting or with real tools. It is mainly for classes and training at schools, hospitals, and factories, as in '현장 실습' and '실습생'.

examples.en: I memorized all the words before the exam.
I memorize song lyrics quickly.

examples.ko: 전화번호를 암기하는 사람이 요즘 별로 없어요.
examples.en: Few people memorize phone numbers these days.

examples.ko: 이 문장을 암기하면 말하기가 쉬울 거예요.
examples.en: If you memorize this sentence, speaking will be easy.
Try to understand instead of just memorizing blindly.
I went having memorized my presentation, but I was still nervous.

explain: '외우다'가 일상에서 훨씬 많이 쓰는 말이고, '암기하다'는 시험 공부나 글에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요. 대화에서는 보통 '단어를 외워요'라고 해요. '암기 과목', '암기력'처럼 합쳐 쓰는 말이 많아요.

phrases.example: 저는 암기력이 좋아서 단어를 빨리 외워요.
phrases.en: I have a good memory, so I learn words quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외우는 힘을 말해요. 시험 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ability to memorize. Often comes up when talking about exams.

phrases.en: History is a memorization subject, so it's hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이해보다 외우는 것이 중요한 과목을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A subject where memorizing matters more than understanding.

phrases.en: I memorized all the song lyrics.
phrases.nuance_ko: '암기하다'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used much more often than 암기하다 in daily talk.

explain_en: In everyday talk Koreans say 외우다 much more often; 암기하다 sounds stiffer and belongs to study and writing. You will hear 단어를 외워요 in conversation. It also appears in compounds like 암기 과목 (a subject learned by rote) and 암기력 (memory ability).

examples.en: I majored in history at university.
We studied the Joseon period in history class.

examples.ko: 역사학과에는 책 읽기를 좋아하는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: The history department has many students who like reading.
My older brother wants to become a historian.
Old records are very important in history studies.
History as a field is hard but interesting.

explain: '역사'는 지나간 일 자체도, 그 일을 연구하는 공부도 가리킬 수 있어요. '역사학'은 학문을 분명하게 말할 때 써요. '심리학', '경제학'처럼 학문 이름에는 '-학'이 많이 붙어요.

phrases.en: My older sister is in the history department at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학에서 역사학을 가르치는 학과예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The university department that teaches history.

phrases.en: He is a famous historian.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사학을 연구하는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who studies history as a field.

phrases.en: I want to study history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학문으로 공부한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means studying it as an academic subject.

explain_en: 역사 can mean past events themselves or the study of them. 역사학 is for naming the academic discipline clearly. Subject names like 심리학 and 경제학 also end in -학.

p.n: Same meaning; 사학 is shorter and a bit more compact in speech.

examples.ko: 선생님이 이번 시험 문제를 어렵게 출제하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher made this exam's questions difficult.

examples.ko: 수학 문제를 출제하는 일은 생각보다 힘들어요.
examples.en: Writing math exam questions is harder than you'd think.
Please pick the words to put on the test.

examples.ko: 기말고사는 수업 시간에 배운 내용에서 출제해요.
examples.en: The final exam questions are drawn from what we learned in class.

examples.ko: 작년에 출제한 문제가 올해 또 나왔어요.
examples.en: A question that was set last year appeared again this year.

examples.ko: 출제하려면 먼저 시험 범위를 알아야 해요.
examples.en: To set the questions, you first need to know the exam scope.

explain: 학생끼리는 '시험에 나오다'를 많이 쓰고, 선생님이 문제를 만드는 쪽은 '출제하다', 학생 입장에서 시험에 나오는 건 '출제되다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '문제를 내다'도 같이 써요.

phrases.en: The teacher will write the exam questions tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출제하다와 같은 뜻으로, 일상 대화에서는 이 말이 더 편하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 출제하다, but it sounds more casual in everyday talk.

phrases.en: This content will appear on the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생 입장에서 문제가 시험에 나온다는 뜻으로 출제하다의 피동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, from a student's view, meaning a question appears on the exam.
phrases.en_equiv: to be set as an exam question

phrases.en: What is the range of the exam?
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 문제가 나올 수 있는 내용의 범위를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The range of content from which exam questions may come.

explain_en: Students usually say 시험에 나오다. The teacher's side, making the questions, is 출제하다, and the student's side, questions appearing on the test, is 출제되다. In daily conversation 문제를 내다 is also used.

examples.ko: 매일 아침 학습지를 한 장씩 풀어요.
examples.en: Every morning I solve one sheet of the workbook.
The worksheet tutor comes to our house.
My younger brother hates the math worksheets.

examples.ko: 이번 달 학습지 값이 너무 비싸요.
examples.en: This month's workbook fee is too expensive.
I lost the worksheet I got as homework.

examples.ko: 학습지를 밀리면 나중에 한꺼번에 해야 해요.
examples.en: If you fall behind on worksheets, you have to do them all at once later.

explain: 한국에서는 집에서 매주 풀고 선생님이 확인해 주는 정기 교재를 '학습지'라고 많이 불러요. 서점에서 사서 푸는 책은 '문제집'이고, 학교에서 한 장씩 나눠 주는 종이는 '유인물'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I do my worksheets every evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '학습지'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most commonly paired with 학습지.

phrases.en: My younger sibling does a subscription workbook every week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정기 학습지를 구독해서 공부한다는 뜻으로 편하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say someone studies with a regular subscription workbook.

phrases.en: I have a lot of worksheet homework today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학습지로 내 주는 숙제를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to homework assigned through the workbook.

explain_en: In Korea, a regular set of materials you solve at home weekly and a tutor checks is commonly called '학습지'. A book you buy at a bookstore to practice is a '문제집', and a sheet handed out at school is also called '유인물'.
